360119.title: Gharakhloo–Welker positive matching conjecture for complete 3-uniform hypergraphs
360119.review_depth: Current source Theorem 1.2 and proof Section 2 give positivity in the residual lexicographically ordered hypergraph, proving the intended Gharakhloo–Welker decomposition conjecture. Proof explicitly removes earlier matchings. MathDB suppresses this residual ambient condition.
360119.mathematical_attempts_and_remaining_gap: The ambient-complete-hypergraph literal wording is not the intended theorem. It also touches credited 366974 family. No credit for a global-versus-residual correction.
360119.literal_statement:
Let $H=(V=[n],E)$ be a complete $3$-uniform hypergraph. For integers $l_1$ and $l_2$, define

$$
E_{l_1,l_2}=\\{\\{a,b,c\\}\in E\mid a<b<c,\ a+b=l_1,\ b+c=l_2\\}.
$$

A subset $M\subseteq E$ is a **positive matching** if it is a matching and there exists a weight function $w:V\to\mathbb{Q}$ such that

$$
\sum_{i\in e}w(i)>0\quad\text{if }e\in M,\qquad \sum_{i\in e}w(i)<0\quad\text{if }e\in E\setminus M.
$$

**Gharakhloo–Welker's conjecture.** For every $3\leq l_1\leq 2n-3$ and $5\leq l_2\leq 2n-1$, $E_{l_1,l_2}$ is a positive matching.

360227.title: The set-uniform Vinogradov mean value conjecture
360227.review_depth: Source introductory conjecture is a uniform bound over all finite integer sets with a constant depending only on s,k,epsilon. The finite-field improvement of the source is not the full integer cardinality-uniform estimate.
360227.mathematical_attempts_and_remaining_gap: A finite numerical value cannot refute a big-O assertion with an unspecified constant. Need a family with unbounded normalized ratio or a uniform analytic estimate.
360227.literal_statement:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be a finite set. For $s,k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $J_{s,k}(A)$ denote the number of solutions $(x_1,\ldots,x_{2s})\in A^{2s}$ to

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{s}(x_i^j-x_{i+s}^j)=0 \qquad (1\leq j\leq k).
$$

**Set-uniform Vinogradov mean value conjecture.** For every real number $\epsilon>0$,

$$
J_{s,k}(A) \ll_{s,k,\epsilon} |A|^{\epsilon}\left(|A|^s+|A|^{2s-k(k+1)/2}\right).
$$

This conjecture would replace the known factor $N^{\epsilon}$ in the corresponding bound for sets $A\subseteq[N]$ by the intrinsic factor $|A|^{\epsilon}$. The $k=1$ case is trivial, but even the $k=2$ case remains open according to the source.
